claim.quote: The bubble chamber has now been shown to have sensitivity to ~1 keV nuclear recoils while remaining insensitive to bubble nucleation by $\gamma$-rays.

key_value.note: Upper limit on the probability of bubble nucleation by gamma-ray-induced Auger cascades at 0.50 keV.
key_value.quote: a limit of $<1.1\times10^{-6}$ set at 0.50 keV

name: Low-threshold response of a scintillating xenon bubble chamber to nuclear and electronic recoils
notes: Result of the xenon bubble chamber operated at Northwestern University, signed 'SBC collaboration' (not an SBC-LAr10 or SBC-SNOLAB measurement).

summary.plain: The same xenon bubble chamber, run at much lower thresholds, still ignored gamma rays while seeing nuclear recoils of about 1 keV, which supports the plan for 100 eV argon chambers.
summary.technical: Thermodynamic thresholds as low as 0.50 keV (hardware limited); calibration of the nuclear-recoil nucleation response versus recoil energy and thermodynamic state; upper limit < 1.1e-6 on the probability of bubble nucleation by gamma-ray Auger cascades at 0.50 keV (Phys. Rev. D 111, 032002).

title: Low-threshold response of a scintillating xenon bubble chamber to nuclear and electronic recoils
why_it_matters: The abstract says the chamber is sensitive to ~1 keV nuclear recoils while insensitive to nucleation by gamma rays.
